description: Hand-curated gold observations for the Fix-4 work, drawn from real reviewer feedback on the extraction pipeline. Unlike tests/gold/observations.json (which anchors to cached-corpus sentence_ids and is scored from the store), these records are self-contained: each carries the sentence text in `sentence_quote`, and the synthetic evaluator (mehungry_extractor.knowledge.goldsynth) builds a one-sentence canonical document from that text, runs the real model-path pipeline, and scores the produced observations with goldeval.score. This lets a coverage change be measured without depending on which papers happen to be in data/corpus. Endpoint `concept_id`/`in_vocab` come from normalize.normalize (verified 2026-09-30). A record whose `expected` list is empty is a *precision* target: a perfect extractor emits nothing (the true argument is a non-entity / anaphor), so anything produced is spurious. `unscorable` expectations are recorded for completeness but skipped by the scorer (they need a predicate or vocabulary entry that does not exist yet).

sentences.sentence_quote: Nutritional care in IBD patients is crucial, focusing on preventing malnutrition, specific micronutrient deficiencies, and adverse changes in body composition.

expected.note: Current output binds IBD as the subject by adjacency (IBD is the population inside 'IBD patients', not the agent). The true subject is the out-of-vocab noun phrase 'Nutritional care', so no claim should form and IBD->prevents->malnutrition must not be emitted.

sentences.sentence_quote: This diet has been shown to offer several benefits to patients in remission, such as reducing inflammation and improving overall health outcomes.
sentences.note: Precision target: the true subject is the anaphor 'This diet' (unresolved) and 'in remission' is a disease_state condition, not the subject. A perfect extractor emits nothing; remission->decreases->inflammation is a fabrication.

sentences.sentence_quote: Consuming 400 mL of kefir once daily for 4 weeks helps regulate gut microbiota, improves abdominal pain, intestinal inflammation, stool frequency, stool consistency, and quality of life in patients.

expected.note: Agent 'kefir' sits in the leading gerund clause; the current binder mis-assigns 'gut microbiota' as subject.

sentences.sentence_quote: Recent studies have shown that fiber consumption has a prebiotic effect, as the metabolites generated by microbiota, such as butyrate, serve as protective factors against IBD activity and decrease the risk of colon cancer.

expected.note: 'serve as protective factors against IBD' -> prevents. Needs the 'protective ... against' cue widening (Phase 4c) and fiber (not IBD) as subject.
'decrease the risk of colon cancer' -> reduces_risk with subject fiber, not IBD.

sentences.sentence_quote: Some dairy foods have been found to contain sulfur-containing products that are harmful to colon cells, as they increase the concentration of hydrogen sulfide in the intestine.

expected.note: Predicate 'increase' lives in a relative clause (needs Phase 4a); object 'concentration of hydrogen sulfide' needs measure-noun unwrapping (Phase 4b); 'in the intestine' is a locative. Both endpoints are out of vocab (end-to-end recall only).

sentences.sentence_quote: Furthermore, an imbalance in the consumption of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids has been linked to increased IBD activity.
sentences.note: Precision target: the true subject is 'an imbalance in the consumption of ...' (a non-entity relational noun). Neither omega-3 nor omega-6 is the subject; a perfect extractor emits nothing.

sentences.sentence_quote: Patients with severe diarrhea (Bristol 7) may require enteral nutrition or intensive hydration strategies to prevent dehydration.

expected.note: Regression guard (reviewer-confirmed correct). 'may ... to prevent' -> prevents / possible.

sentences.sentence_quote: Moreover, inflammation induces dysbiosis, characterized by alterations in the composition and function of the gut microbiota.

object.text: alterations in the composition and function of the gut microbiota

expected.note: Phase 15 (reviewer-confirmed correct). The reduced relative 'characterized by ...' is a descriptive child of the 'induces' relation: its implicit subject is the governing object (dysbiosis) and its object is the WHOLE descriptor phrase 'alterations in the composition and function of the gut microbiota' - not the deep entity 'gut microbiota', which would assert the wrong thing. The phrase is a free-text descriptor (no concept id), so it is scorable for precision but out-of-vocab for achievable recall. Nests beneath inflammation->causes->dysbiosis.

sentences.sentence_quote: Specifically, red meat has been associated with a higher risk of developing IBD.

expected.note: Regression guard (reviewer-confirmed correct). 'associated with a higher risk of' -> increases_risk.

sentences.sentence_quote: The Mediterranean diet reduces the consumption of red meat and processed meat.
sentences.note: Phase 4b coverage anchor: the object head 'consumption' is a measure noun; both coordinated endpoints in its 'of' phrase must be unwrapped. Without unwrapping only the head-most ('red meat') binds.

sentences.sentence_quote: Dietary fiber acts as a protective factor against colorectal cancer.
sentences.note: Phase 4c coverage anchor: 'protective factor against' (a noun between 'protective' and 'against') must map to prevents, not be missed.

sentences.sentence_quote: The Mediterranean diet is linked to a lower risk of cardiovascular diseases and chronic conditions.

expected.note: Needs an association-with-risk predicate (Fix 3): 'linked to a lower risk of' must promote away from bare associated_with.

sentences.sentence_quote: In IBD patients, there is a growing body of research recommending reducing the intake of red meat, processed meat, and saturated fats.

expected.note: Needs a deontic predicate (Phase 4d) plus measure-noun unwrapping of 'intake of X, Y, and Z' (Phase 4b) and clausal-complement predicate discovery (Phase 4a).

sentences.sentence_quote: It has been reported that a higher intake of omega-6 fatty acids is associated with a greater risk of developing UC.

expected.note: Needs the association-with-risk predicate (Fix 3) and 'UC' in the disease vocabulary.
